narrative:
The model determined that you have a 31% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the threshold the bank uses, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were your savings, the purpose of the loan, and the status of your checking account. Your substantial savings of over 1,000 DM was the strongest positive factor and pushed the prediction strongly toward approval. However, two other details worked against you and ultimately outweighed that advantage.

Requesting the loan to buy a new car pulled the prediction toward higher risk. Among approved applicants, only 16.5% used the money for a new car, while far more received loans for radio/TV or furniture. In addition, having a checking-account balance between 0 and 200 DM also increased the risk score. Only 18% of approved customers show this exact balance range, whereas most approved applicants have no checking account at all.

Taken together, the purpose of the loan and your checking-account status created enough concern to overcome the protective effect of your large savings, leading to the denial.

You should next focus on paying down any existing small balances so your checking account moves into a cleaner range, or consider applying for a smaller loan to purchase a used car or for home improvements instead. Either change would likely improve your chances on a future application. (248 words)
